back: A temporary initiative in a unique context undertaken to create value.

front: What does 'temporary' mean for a project?
back: The work has a defined beginning and end. It does not mean short, and the deliverables often persist after the project ends.
The specific conditions that distinguish one project from another, even similar ones: goals, scope, location, technology, risks, resources, stakeholders.

front: Five conditions under which a project ends
back: Objectives achieved; objectives will not or cannot be met; resources exhausted; the need no longer exists; terminated for legal, regulatory or other reasons.
Applying knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to project activities to meet or exceed the intended value.
Adding features or extras nobody requested. Not endorsed: 'exceeding value' does not mean extra scope.
The person assigned by the performing organization to lead the team responsible for achieving the project objectives.

front: Project team vs project management team
back: Project team: everyone performing the project work. Project management team: the members directly involved in project management activities.
Project management office: an organizational entity that centralizes activities related to managing portfolios, programs and/or projects.
A group of related projects and program activities managed in a coordinated manner to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually.
Programs, projects and operations managed as a group to maximize value delivery and achieve strategic objectives, meet obligations, or generate income.

front: Do the components of a portfolio have to be related?
back: No. Components of a program are related; components of a portfolio only share the link to strategy.
Selecting, prioritizing, managing and optimizing programs and projects in line with strategic goals.
Efficient, ongoing production of products and services, turning inputs into outputs. Outside the scope of a project.
A product, result or service generated by a process. May be an input to a successor process.
The end result or consequence of a process or project. Can be positive (benefit) or negative (disbenefit).
Benefit: a gain realized from outcomes. Disbenefit: an unintended negative consequence or loss.
The excess of financial and non-financial benefits over the investment. Different stakeholders perceive it differently.
A document or other item created to help manage a portfolio, program or project and to inform the team and stakeholders.
The strategic business activities that build, sustain or advance an organization: portfolios, programs, projects, products and operations.
1) Success of project outcomes: was the intended value realized? 2) Success of project management: were cost, scope, time and quality constraints met?

front: Current state, transition state, future state
back: A project moves the organization from where it is now (current) to the desired result (future), sometimes through planned intermediate steps (transition).
